name: Starport Encounter Type
description: p.60. Roll 1D every six hours (or every 1D hours) spent exploring a starport. A legal encounter can be avoided by rolling equal to or over the local world’s law level on 2D + SOC DM of the spacer with the lowest SOC score in the group.

results.text: Legal encounter: This type of encounter involves the spacers being approached, questioned, or asked for permits from local law enforcement, custom agents, or security. These encounters can be avoided by rolling equal to or over the local world’s law level on the 2D + SOC DM of the spacer with the lowest SOC score in the group. Apply the NPC reaction table on pg. 56 to any legal encounters. If a legal encounter does occur, the spacers can avoid arrest, fines, etc. by making the same check again.
General encounter: A general starport encounter is generated by rolling a D66 on the encounter table.

name: Starport Encounter Table
description: The Toolkit's starport encounter applies the starport and government DMs to the tens die for you. p.61. Roll D66 with the DM applied to the tens die (add DM × 10 to the total). Results run from 01 to 96. DMs (Starport Encounter Modification Table, p.60; combine both): Starport A +2, B +1, C +0, D -1, E -2, X -3. Government code 0: -2; 2, 4, 8: -1; 1, 3, 5: +0; 6, 7, 9: +1; A, B, C: +2; D, E, F: +3. Example: Starport B (+1) with Captive Government (+1) gives +2, a range of 31-86. BOOK: the book's example says +3 and 41-96, which does not match its own DMs. Ranges: 01-06 abandoned or neglected, 11-16 seedy, 21-26 rundown, 31-36 out of date, 41-46 below average, 51-56 average, 61-66 above average, 71-76 elite, 81-86 prohibitive, 91-96 oppressive. For a random NPC range such as 31-56, roll D3 to choose the 10 interval (1 = 31-36, 2 = 41-46, 3 = 51-56).
